name: Judas Iscariot
charge: Theft from the common purse; betraying innocent blood for thirty pieces of silver
summary: One of the twelve, he carried the bag and took what was put in it, and his objection to the ointment at Bethany was made in the name of the poor although he cared nothing for them (John 12:4-6). Satan entered into him, he asked the chief priests what they would give him, they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver as the prophet had written, and he delivered Christ with a kiss (Luke 22:3-6; Zechariah 11:12-13; Luke 22:47-48). When he saw that Christ was condemned he brought the money back, confessed that he had betrayed innocent blood, threw the silver into the temple and hanged himself (Matthew 27:3-5).
offenseFull: He was one of the twelve and he kept the bag, which is where the money was, and he took what was put in it (John 12:4-6; John 13:29). His objection to Mary’s ointment at Bethany was spoken in the name of the poor, and John says plainly that it was not because he cared for the poor, but because he was a thief. He walked with Christ, saw the healing, was around the commandment keeping, and never repented of what he was. The commandment on it is one line: do not steal (Exodus 20:15). Riches are not comely for a niggard, and what should an envious man do with money (Ecclesiasticus 14:3)? They that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts which drown men in destruction and perdition, for the love of money is the root of all evil, and some coveting after it have erred from the faith and pierced themselves through with many sorrows (1 Timothy 6:9-10).

Then Satan entered into him, and he went to the chief priests and captains and asked what they would give him, and they were glad and covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver, and from that time he sought opportunity to betray him away from the multitude (Luke 22:3-6; Matthew 26:14-16). Men are not in their right mind when they can be glad over a thing like that. The price was written beforehand: thirty pieces of silver, cast to the potter in the house of the Lord (Zechariah 11:12-13), which Matthew credits to Jeremy because Zechariah was repeating what the earlier prophet had said in a writing that did not survive. Judas delivered him with a kiss, and was asked whether he betrayed the Son of man with a kiss (Luke 22:47-48). The statute names the act without disguise: cursed is the man that takes reward to slay an innocent person (Deuteronomy 27:25), and the psalm had said it would be the familiar friend who lifted up his heel (Psalms 41:9).
judgmentFull: When he saw that Christ was condemned, he repented himself, brought the thirty pieces of silver back to the chief priests and elders and said he had sinned in that he had betrayed innocent blood; they told him to see to it himself, and he cast the silver down in the temple, departed, and went and hanged himself (Matthew 27:3-5). Giving the money back did not give back the life he had sold. The priests would not put it into the treasury because it was the price of blood, and bought the potter’s field with it to bury strangers in, so that the field is called the field of blood to this day (Matthew 27:6-10). Acts records the fearful end there and the office given to another man, as the psalm had said (Acts 1:16-20; Acts 1:25; Psalms 109:8).

The warning had been spoken at the table: the Son of man goes as it is written of him, but woe to that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed, and it had been good for that man if he had never been born (Mark 14:21; Matthew 26:24). He was sorry afterward, and sorrow by itself is not repentance: godly sorrow works repentance to salvation not to be repented of, but the sorrow of the world works death (2 Corinthians 7:10). He that loves gold shall not be justified, and gold has been the ruin of many, their destruction being present with them (Ecclesiasticus 31:5-6). A place among the twelve, three years in the company of Christ and the trust of the bag did not make a hidden covetousness safe. Money was his demise, and men will still give a brother up for it.

lawsResolved.text: You are not to take a gift or money offered as a bribe.
They are cursed who take reward against the innocent.
You shall not steal another's property.
You shall not deal falsely or treacherously with your brethren.
Shedding of innocent blood is an abomination to God.
Killing for hire is condemned (the assassin and the one who hires him are both guilty of murder).
The love of money is the root of all evil, and causes one to wander from the faith.

text.text: Then saith one of his disciples, Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, which should betray him,
Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred pence, and given to the poor?
This he said, not that he cared for the poor; but because he was a thief, and had the bag, and bare what was put therein.
For some of them thought, because Judas had the bag, that Jesus had said unto him, Buy those things that we have need of against the feast; or, that he should give something to the poor.
Thou shalt not steal.
Riches are not comely for a niggard: and what should an envious man do with money?
But they that will be rich fall into temptation and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful lusts, which drown men in destruction and perdition.
For the love of money is the root of all evil: which while some coveted after, they have erred from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
Then entered Satan into Judas surnamed Iscariot, being of the number of the twelve.
And he went his way, and communed with the chief priests and captains, how he might betray him unto them.
And they were glad, and covenanted to give him money.
And he promised, and sought opportunity to betray him unto them in the absence of the multitude.
Then one of the twelve, called Judas Iscariot, went unto the chief priests,
And said unto them, What will ye give me, and I will deliver him unto you? And they covenanted with him for thirty pieces of silver.
And from that time he sought opportunity to betray him.
And I said unto them, If ye think good, give me my price; and if not, forbear. So they weighed for my price thirty pieces of silver.
And the Lord said unto me, Cast it unto the potter: a goodly price that I was prised at of them. And I took the thirty pieces of silver, and cast them to the potter in the house of the Lord.
And while he yet spake, behold a multitude, and he that was called Judas, one of the twelve, went before them, and drew near unto Jesus to kiss him.
But Jesus said unto him, Judas, betrayest thou the Son of man with a kiss?
Cursed be he that taketh reward to slay an innocent person. And all the people shall say, Amen.
Yea, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted, which did eat of my bread, hath lifted up his heel against me.
Then Judas, which had betrayed him, when he saw that he was condemned, repented himself, and brought again the thirty pieces of silver to the chief priests and elders,
Saying, I have sinned in that I have betrayed the innocent blood. And they said, What is that to us? see thou to that.
And he cast down the pieces of silver in the temple, and departed, and went and hanged himself.
And the chief priests took the silver pieces, and said, It is not lawful for to put them into the treasury, because it is the price of blood.
And they took counsel, and bought with them the potter’s field, to bury strangers in.
Wherefore that field was called, The field of blood, unto this day.
Then was fulfilled that which was spoken by Jeremy the prophet, saying, And they took the thirty pieces of silver, the price of him that was valued, whom they of the children of Israel did value;
And gave them for the potter’s field, as the Lord appointed me.
Men and brethren, this scripture must needs have been fulfilled, which the Holy Ghost by the mouth of David spake before concerning Judas, which was guide to them that took Jesus.
For he was numbered with us, and had obtained part of this ministry.
Now this man purchased a field with the reward of iniquity; and falling headlong, he burst asunder in the midst, and all his bowels gushed out.
And it was known unto all the dwellers at Jerusalem; insomuch as that field is called in their proper tongue, Aceldama, that is to say, The field of blood.
For it is written in the book of Psalms, Let his habitation be desolate, and let no man dwell therein: and his bishoprick let another take.
That he may take part of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas by transgression fell, that he might go to his own place.
Let his days be few; and let another take his office.
The Son of man indeed goeth, as it is written of him: but woe to that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! good were it for that man if he had never been born.
The Son of man goeth as it is written of him: but woe unto that man by whom the Son of man is betrayed! it had been good for that man if he had not been born.
For godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.
He that loveth gold shall not be justified, and he that followeth corruption shall have enough thereof.
Gold hath been the ruin of many, and their destruction was present.
And supper being ended, the devil having now put into the heart of Judas Iscariot, Simon’s son, to betray him;
And while he yet spake, lo, Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swords and staves, from the chief priests and elders of the people.
Now he that betrayed him gave them a sign, saying, Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he: hold him fast.
And forthwith he came to Jesus, and said, Hail, master; and kissed him.
And Jesus said unto him, Friend, wherefore art thou come? Then came they, and laid hands on Jesus, and took him.
